units.text: INT. GHOSTS - CONTINUOUS
Regina could have been got to do it.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: I don't understand you. What is this about dread--and Regina?
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Is it very late, mother?
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: It is early morning.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: She looks out through the conservatory.
The day is dawning over the mountains. And the weather is clearing, Oswald. In a little while you shall see the sun.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: I'm glad of that. Oh, I may still have much to rejoice in and live for--
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: I should think so, indeed!
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Even if I can't work--
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Oh, you'll soon be able to work again, my dear boy--now that you haven't got all those gnawing and depressing thoughts to brood over any longer.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Yes, I'm glad you were able to rid me of all those fancies. And when I've got over this one thing more--
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Sits on the sofa.
Now we will have a little talk, mother--
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Yes, let us.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: She pushes an arm-chair towards the sofa, and sits down close to him.
And meantime the sun will be rising. And then you will know all. And then I shall not feel this dread any longer.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: What is it that I am to know?
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Not listening to her.
Mother, did you not say a little while ago, that there was nothing in the world you would not do for me, if I asked you?
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Yes, indeed I said so!
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: And you'll stick to it, mother?
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: You may rely on that, my dear and only boy! I have nothing in the world to live for but you alone.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Very well, then; now you shall hear--Mother, you have a strong, steadfast mind, I know. Now you're to sit quite still when you hear it.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: What dreadful thing can it be--?
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: You're not to scream out. Do you hear? Do you promise me that? We will sit and talk about it quietly. Do you promise me, mother?
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Yes, yes; I promise. Only speak!
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Well, you must know that all this fatigue--and my inability to think of work--all that is not the illness itself--
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Then what is the illness itself?
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: The disease I have as my birthright--
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: He points to his forehead and adds very softly.
--is seated here.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Almost voiceless.
Oswald! No--no!
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Don't scream. I can't bear it. Yes, mother, it is seated here waiting. And it may break out any day--at any moment.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Oh, what horror--!
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Now, quiet, quiet. That is how it stands with me--
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Springs up.
It's not true, Oswald! It's impossible! It cannot be so!
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: I have had one attack down there already. It was soon over. But when I came to know the state I had been in, then the dread descended upon me, raging and ravening; and so I set off home to you as fast as I could.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Then this is the dread--!
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Yes--it's so indescribably loathsome, you know. Oh, if it had only been an ordinary mortal disease--! For I'm not so afraid of death--though I should like to live as long as I can.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Yes, yes, Oswald, you must!
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: But this is so unutterably loathsome. To become a little baby again! To have to be fed! To have to--Oh, it's not to be spoken of!
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: The child has his mother to nurse him.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Springs up.
